runner: by hand after a change to the SFTP provider, the endpoint race, the host-key gate or remote recipient slots
reason: builds the worker repository's devserve (the real SFTP stack, read-only, on a throw-away data directory) and runs SftpLiveTests against it over a real SSH connection - the only proof that the provider's exception classification, host-key hook and download are what SSH.NET really does, and that a document the Share Manager's own code produced imports and opens. It also builds tests/Integration/rwsftp offline from the Go module cache (a writable pkg/sftp server, files in memory, 127.0.0.1 only) and runs RemoteSlotLiveTests against it - the write path of a recipient slot that names a server folder (007 section 4.2). Optional -SmbShare runs read-only current-account listing/download/lease checks and preserves an existing Windows connection on the explicitly supplied share; two-user credential-prompt acceptance remains separate. It needs Go and the worker repository, builds a binary and opens a listening socket, so it is never part of a default or -Integration run; it never starts the worker or touches its pipe or data directory, and without Go or the repository it reports COULD NOT VERIFY
